nodes.label: Mid-1950s cotton procurement and coupon-based cloth access
Limited disposable household cash in Zhouzhi accounts
Purchased factory cloth for household clothing
Guanzhong household spinning, weaving and clothing work
Women operators’ available time and rest
Household expectations that women provide clothing

edges.qualification: Formal access required allocation and purchase; this edge records restricted channels, not a net effect compared with no rationing. Rationing also distributed entitlements.

scope.configuration: Named Guanzhong villages and Zhouzhi work/consumption accounts under mid-1950s procurement and later collective arrangements; not all China.

alternatives: Different ration/income policies are counterfactual, not observed treatments
edges.dispute: No identified overall policy effect: ration quantity, cash, prices and household needs interact.

edges.qualification: Interviewees linked coupon resale/nonpurchase to scarce disposable cash. A ration coupon was not itself a purchased garment.

scope.configuration: Named Guanzhong villages and Zhouzhi work/consumption accounts under mid-1950s procurement and later collective arrangements; not all China.

alternatives: Obtain gifts or other household resources
edges.dispute: Social role and cloth quality differ between reported buyers and nonsellers; no matched comparison.

edges.qualification: Retained, concealed or exchanged cotton supplied inputs for reported home production; legal retention did not describe all actual access.

scope.configuration: Named Guanzhong villages and Zhouzhi work/consumption accounts under mid-1950s procurement and later collective arrangements; not all China.

alternatives: Purchased cloth substitutes for home processing
edges.dispute: Input quantities and channel shares are not independently audited; no single channel is claimed necessary.

edges.qualification: Reported household expectations added clothing duties to women’s existing claims on time. This is not a claim that those expectations were necessary or sufficient for home production.

scope.configuration: Named Guanzhong villages and Zhouzhi work/consumption accounts under mid-1950s procurement and later collective arrangements; not all China.

alternatives: Shared or collective services where effective
edges.dispute: Authority, affection, skill and scarcity overlap; no causal share or universal household rule.

edges.qualification: Collective field duties competed for time also needed for domestic work and rest.

scope.configuration: Named Guanzhong villages and Zhouzhi work/consumption accounts under mid-1950s procurement and later collective arrangements; not all China.

alternatives: Reduced collective hours or reassignment where permitted
edges.dispute: Retrospective accounts do not yield a complete comparable time-use panel or prove identical obligations for every woman.

edges.qualification: Accounts describe additional unpaid textile work reducing available rest after other duties; the burden is scoped to the reported configuration.

scope.configuration: Named Guanzhong villages and Zhouzhi work/consumption accounts under mid-1950s procurement and later collective arrangements; not all China.

alternatives: Reduce clothing service or other work
edges.dispute: Not an inherent effect of hand weaving in all settings; these alternatives were not equally feasible.

edges.qualification: Home textile work provided clothing and social textile goods in the local accounts, while imposing distinct operator costs.

scope.configuration: Named Guanzhong villages and Zhouzhi work/consumption accounts under mid-1950s procurement and later collective arrangements; not all China.

edges.dispute: A productive contribution does not demonstrate a voluntary or compensated livelihood, or a technical necessity.
